description:
Hey peps! 👋.

For the NASA Space Apps Challenge, I’m interested in developing an Astronaut Health Monitoring System to support astronauts’ physical and mental well-being during space missions. 

I’m looking for enthusiastic teammates with skills or interests in Python, AI/ML, data analysis, web or app development, UI/UX design, and space science research. 

Let’s combine our ideas and build something impactful for space exploration. 🚀
summary:
During deep-space exploration to Mars and the Moon, astronauts face extreme isolation, radiation, altered gravity, and communication latencies of 14 to 22 minutes each way—making real-time consultation with Earth-based flight surgeons impossible during medical emergencies. 

To solve this challenge, we developed MARK XI: an autonomous, 100% offline-capable Clinical Decision Support System (CDSS) and visual astronaut health monitoring platform. Built upon the NASA Human Research Program (HRP) guidelines and the R.I.D.G.E. spaceflight hazard framework, MARK XI empowers astronauts to detect early physiological deterioration, perform guided ultrasound and vision self-examinations, simulate emergency resuscitations with zero-G CPR pacing, monitor radiation drug half-life decay, and autonomously deploy clinical countermeasures without relying on ground control.
details:
1. WHAT EXACTLY DOES IT DO?

MARK XI provides astronauts with an autonomous, real-time medical monitoring and diagnostic cockpit for deep space exploration missions. It continuously tracks multi-system physiological data across 6 anatomical systems (Cardiovascular, Neuro-Ocular, Musculoskeletal, Renal, Respiratory, and Immune), detects anomalies caused by the 5 hazards of spaceflight (Radiation, Isolation, Distance, Gravity, Hostile Environments), guides astronauts through clinical self-examinations, and calculates immediate treatment protocols offline.

2. HOW DOES IT WORK?

- Touchless Optical Biometrics: Leverages webcam-based remote Photoplethysmography (rPPG) and PERCLOS eye-blink tracking to detect cardiac variability and cognitive microsleep without wearable sensors.

- Digital Twin 3D Bio-Avatar: Renders an interactive physiological model featuring real-time laser scanlines and anatomical layer filters (Neuro-Ocular, Circulatory, Musculoskeletal).

- J.A.R.V.I.S. Offline AI Flight Surgeon: Provides a local differential diagnostic engine with hands-free speech recognition and audio synthesis that diagnoses symptoms and prescribes NASA HRP countermeasures during Earth communication blackouts.

- S.T.E.A.L.T.H. Hands-Free Voice Assistant: Allows astronauts wearing bulky EVA or IVA suits to operate telemetry feeds, trigger triage, and navigate modules completely hands-free.

- Space Pharmacy & Radiation Degradation Engine: Simulates galactic cosmic ray (GCR) radiolysis of active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs), auto-calculates clinical dose offsets (+15% to +20%), and triggers on-demand 3D drug synthesis.

- CODE RED Emergency Action System: Features an interactive 110-BPM Zero-G CPR metronome with visual compression guidance calibrated to NASA Flight Rule B13-102 (Crew Medical Restraint System), accompanied by emergency sirens and step-by-step triage for cardiac arrest, decompression, ammonia leaks, and solar particle events.

- Form 1047-B Medical Dossier & PRACA Dispatch: One-click export of clinical flight summaries and NASA Form 1048-A problem reporting for Deep Space Network (DSN) uplink.

3. WHAT BENEFITS DOES IT HAVE?

- Eliminates dependency on ground control during critical 14–22 minute communication delays.

- Prevents spaceflight-induced permanent disabilities, including SANS (Spaceflight-Associated Neuro-Ocular Syndrome) and severe bone demineralization (-1.1% per month).

- Protects crew psychological health through circadian blue-light scheduling (460nm) and synthesized 432 Hz Earth Biophilia audio immersion.

- Reduces medical payload mass by enabling targeted pharmaceutical dose adjustments and simulated on-demand medicine replenishment.

4. WHAT DO WE HOPE TO ACHIEVE?

Our vision is to provide an operational flight baseline for NASA's Artemis Lunar Basecamp, Deep Space Gateway, and Crewed Mars Expedition missions—ensuring astronaut survival and mission autonomy when Earth is just a distant point of light. Furthermore, the lightweight, offline architecture directly translates to terrestrial remote medicine (polar research stations, deep-sea vessels, and disaster relief zones).

5. TOOLS, CODING LANGUAGES, HARDWARE & SOFTWARE USED:

- Languages & Core: JavaScript (ES6+), HTML5 Canvas (Hardware-accelerated ECG cardiac trace & AR mesh), CSS3.

- Framework: React 18, Vite 6, Tailwind CSS (Custom NASA HUD glassmorphism theme).

- 3D & Visualization: Three.js (Interactive GLTF/GLB astronaut digital twin), Recharts (BMD decay curves, circadian telemetry, biodosimetry).

- Audio & Speech Processing: Web Audio API (110-BPM Zero-G CPR metronome, space klaxon alarm, spatial nature soundscapes), Web Speech Recognition API (Hands-Free Voice-to-Text), Web Speech Synthesis API (J.A.R.V.I.S. voice output).

- Computer Vision: WebRTC MediaDevices API (rPPG touchless vitals & PERCLOS fatigue monitoring).

- Version Control & Deployment: Git, GitHub, Vite Client-Side PWA architecture.

FULL WORKING AND DISCRIPTION ATTACHED IN SOURCE: https://github.com/thv77/PROJECT-XI
